segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Naaman was a great man. Captain of the armies of Syria, honorable, mighty in valour. And under all that armor — he was a leper.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In his house served a young girl carried captive out of Israel. She knew where healing was.

segments.speaker: woman
segments.text: Would God my lord were with the prophet that is in Samaria! for he would recover him of his leprosy.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So Naaman came — with his horses, his chariots, his silver and gold — and stood at the door of a plain little house. The prophet didn't even come out. He sent a messenger.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: Go and wash in Jordan seven times, and thy flesh shall come again to thee, and thou shalt be clean.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And Naaman was furious. He had expected something great — a mighty ceremony worthy of a mighty man. It was too plain. Too simple. He turned and rode away in a rage.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: If the prophet had bid thee do some great thing, wouldest thou not have done it? how much rather then, when he saith to thee, Wash, and be clean?

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the great captain went down, and dipped himself in the Jordan. Once. Twice. Seven times, exactly as the man of God had said.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And his flesh came again like unto the flesh of a little child, and he was clean.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The instruction wasn't beneath him. It was the way back. If you've been away, the way back may look almost too simple — pray again, read again, come back again. Do the simple thing.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He almost rode away from his healing because it sounded too simple. Do the simple thing.
